routes.description: Establish that agency and rational normativity cannot be reduced to causal compulsion, then use Bradleyan idealism to place lawful explanation within a wider experiential reality.
routes.successCriteria: Show that determinist inference does not eliminate agential sourcehood or relevant modal alternatives and that idealism integrates domains that reductive naturalism leaves unexplained.

motionBridge.description: Libertarian idealism must preserve meaningful agency under lawful description while providing a more comprehensive account of experience than naturalistic reduction.

centralBridges.description: Distinguish mathematical or logical determination from causal compulsion and explain why the former need not displace agents as sources.
Supply an account of alternative possibility and sourcehood that does not depend upon a presently branching physical timeline.
Show why scientific representation is one mode within experience rather than an exhaustive inventory of reality.
Explain how truth, value, feeling, and inquiry can be integrated without reducing them to abstract thought alone.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Connect indispensable responsibility practices to a real distinction between agency and mere bodily occurrence.
Identify experiential, practical, and intellectual constraints that prevent idealism from collapsing into arbitrary invention.

routes.description: Maintain determinist pressure on libertarian alternatives while reconstructing freedom and inquiry through their practical functions without requiring Bradleyan metaphysics.
routes.successCriteria: Show that changing causal vocabulary or modal scope does not secure libertarian freedom, and that pragmatic standards preserve responsibility and disciplined inquiry more economically.

motionBridge.description: Compatibilist pragmatism must retain action-guiding freedom and standards of inquiry while showing that libertarian idealism adds no necessary explanatory gain.

centralBridges.description: Establish that fixed laws and states threaten genuine alternatives even when the determining relation is described as non-causal.
Test whether varying pasts or laws answers the fixed-premise consequence challenge or merely changes the relevant possible worlds.
Explain freedom through the practical distinctions needed for incentives, responsibility, praise, and blame under determinism.
Provide disciplined pragmatic standards for experience-centered inquiry without committing to a substantially existent absolute.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish perspectival or mind-framed access to reality from voluntary construction or mind-controlled truth.
Retain methodological pluralism while specifying constraints that exclude both scientistic reduction and unrestricted inclusion.

sections.title: Determinism, causation, and agential sourcehood
sections.rationale: This issue contains the motion's primary clash over whether complete lawful determination amounts to causal constraint and whether agency can remain explanatorily fundamental.

sections.title: Alternative possibilities and the consequence argument
sections.rationale: The modal scope of doing otherwise determines whether libertarian freedom survives a fixed timeline and whether sourcehood can be separated from control over past facts and laws.

sections.title: Practical responsibility and metaphysical agency
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether freedom's indispensable social functions are sufficient for compatibilism or instead presuppose a deeper distinction between genuine action and bodily occurrence.

sections.title: Experience, science, and naturalistic reduction
sections.rationale: The comparative metaphysical burden turns on whether science exhausts reality, whether other experiential domains require systematic inclusion, and whether a restrained naturalistic idealism can include experience.

sections.title: The absolute and the completion of inquiry
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether Bradleyan integration names a real completion that grounds inquiry or only an aspirational ideal whose substantial existence remains unestablished.
